nodes.title: Worldseed indie-game UI: readable fonts, centered dialog, full-screen background
nodes.body:
Context: the captured screen at http://localhost:5173/ shows the intro as unstyled black text on a white page (IntroScreen uses class intro-screen, which has no CSS). During play, GameLayout puts the story text in a narrow right-hand sidebar (3fr/1fr grid) instead of over the scene. Desired behavior: readable fonts, story text in a centered dialog, and a full-screen background on both the intro and the game. Expected result: a player sees a styled full-screen backdrop with a centered framed dialog at intro and during play. Why: usability and polish.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given the app loads, when the intro shows, then it fills the viewport with a background image and the text sits in a centered framed dialog using the pixel fonts.
- Given the game is playing, when the screen renders, then the scene fills the whole viewport and the story text appears in a centered dialog rather than a right-hand sidebar.
- Given any screen, when text renders, then body text uses VT323 at 16px or larger and headings use Press Start 2P on a dark background with light text.


## Scope
- In scope: Global base typography and colours
- In scope: IntroScreen styling
- In scope: GameLayout full-screen scene and centered story dialog
- In scope: StoryPanel readability inside the dialog
- Out of scope: Backend or API changes
- Out of scope: New art assets
- Out of scope: Admin console styling
- Out of scope: Phaser scene logic and game content
- Preserve: Existing game state, dialogue choices and inventory behavior
- Preserve: HeaderOverlay and ContributionSheet behavior
- Preserve: Existing @fontsource font imports in main.tsx
- Preserve: Frame kit classes sf-frame-* and sf-btn


## Technical constraints
- UI-only change in game/frontend; no API changes
- Use the existing tokens (--sf-color-*, --sf-font-*, --sf-size-*) and frame kit; do not add remote font URLs


## Definition of done
- All requirement slices are implemented and their unit tests pass


## Non-functional requirements
- Text contrast stays readable (light parchment text on dark ink)


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Global readable pixel typography on a dark background
nodes.body:
Context: styles.css only declares CSS variables and frame classes; body has no background, colour or font size, so unstyled pages render black on white in the default font look. Desired behavior: a base layer that sets background, text colour, VT323 body at 20px and Press Start 2P headings. Expected result: all screens are readable by default. Why: readability.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given styles.css, when parsed, then body sets background to var(--sf-color-ink-1) and color to var(--sf-color-parchment-5).
- Given styles.css, when parsed, then body uses font-family var(--sf-font-body) with font-size 20px and h1, h2 use var(--sf-font-pixel).


## Scope
- In scope: Base layer rules in styles.css
- Out of scope: Component-specific styling
- Preserve: Existing --background/--foreground variables
- Preserve: Frame kit rules


## Technical constraints
- Reference token variables defined by tokensToCssVars in src/lib/tokens.ts


## Definition of done
- Base rules exist in styles.css and the unit test passes


## Non-functional requirements
- VT323 is small at default size, so base size is 20px


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Intro screen is a full-screen backdrop with a centered framed dialog
nodes.body:
Context: IntroScreen.tsx renders four plain paragraphs and a bare button in section.intro-screen with no styling. Desired behavior: full-screen background and a centered framed dialog with a gold Begin button. Expected result: the first screen looks like an indie game title card. Why: first impression and usability.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given IntroScreen renders, when inspected, then the root has class sf-fullscreen-bg and contains a centered dialog with class sf-frame-parchment.
- Given IntroScreen renders, when the Begin button is clicked, then onBegin is called once and the four intro lines are still present.


## Scope
- In scope: IntroScreen markup and classes
- In scope: CSS for sf-fullscreen-bg and sf-dialog
- Out of scope: New artwork
- Out of scope: Changing intro copy
- Preserve: Intro text lines
- Preserve: Begin button accessible name 'Begin'
- Preserve: onBegin prop


## Technical constraints
- Use existing wall.png under /assets/worlds/the-boys-room/room as the backdrop
- Use Frame and Button components from components/ui


## Dependencies
- R1


## Definition of done
- IntroScreen shows a backdrop and centered dialog and its unit test passes


## Non-functional requirements
- image-rendering pixelated on the backdrop


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Gameplay scene fills the viewport and story text sits in a centered dialog
nodes.body:
Context: GameLayout.tsx uses grid-cols md:[3fr_1fr] with an aside drawer and Story toggle button. Desired behavior: the scene main fills the viewport and the story prop renders inside a centered dialog overlay. Expected result: text appears centered over a full-screen scene. Why: the requested indie-game look.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given GameLayout renders scene, header and story, when inspected, then no aside element exists and the main scene container has class h-screen w-full.
- Given GameLayout renders, when inspected, then the story node is inside an element with data-testid story-dialog and class sf-dialog that is centered and the scene stays mounted.


## Scope
- In scope: GameLayout structure and classes
- In scope: Removing the sidebar and drawer toggle from GameLayout
- In scope: Updating obsolete layout tests
- Out of scope: uiStore drawer fields
- Out of scope: Phaser sizing logic
- Preserve: header, scene and story props
- Preserve: PhaserHost fills its container
- Preserve: HeaderOverlay position


## Technical constraints
- The dialog wrapper must be pointer-events-none with a pointer-events-auto dialog so scene objects stay clickable
- Scene stays rendered by App through the scene prop


## Dependencies
- R2


## Definition of done
- Sidebar path removed and dialog layout unit tests pass


## Non-functional requirements
- Dialog max height 60vh and scrolls internally


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · StoryPanel is dialog content with larger readable text
nodes.body:
Context: StoryPanel.tsx root is sf-frame-panel h-full text-sm sized for a narrow sidebar, with bare h1/h2 and small text. Desired behavior: content sized for a centered dialog: sf-dialog body text, speaker in pixel font, choices as full-width gold buttons. Expected result: dialogue is easy to read. Why: readability.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given StoryPanel renders a node, when inspected, then the root keeps class story-content and has no h-full or text-sm class.
- Given a node with two choices, when rendered, then each choice button has class w-full and the speaker heading has class font-pixel.


## Scope
- In scope: StoryPanel classes and markup
- Out of scope: Dialogue logic
- Out of scope: Inventory slot data
- Preserve: aria-labels Dialogue, Choices, Event log, Story history, Inventory
- Preserve: Portrait image
- Preserve: onChoose behavior


## Technical constraints
- Keep the story-content root class (asserted by existing tests)


## Dependencies
- R3


## Definition of done
- StoryPanel readable classes applied and unit tests pass


## Non-functional requirements
- Text size at least 16px


## Clarifying questions
- None
